channel.title: arab_news (frozen sample, trimmed to what we store)

item.title: UNIFIL records 2,840 Israeli artillery shells, 90 airstrikes in southern Lebanon in October alone
item.description: BEIRUT: The United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) said Friday that Israeli violations continued across southern Lebanon in October, including airstrikes and artillery shelling targeting several towns and villages.

item.title: Literary adventure
item.description: Explore a series of character-inspired homes at Dhahran Expo where children follow clues, solve challenges and discover the well-known literary figures behind each space. Find out more on ithra.com.

item.title: Bounce world
item.description: The Big Bounce Arabia features giant inflatables, obstacle courses, slides, interactive zones and refreshment areas for all ages. Inspired by The Big Bounce America, it is organized by Benchmark and you can find more details at webook.com.

item.title: Interactive show
item.description: Discover Ms. Rachel World — Tribute Show at Wonder Garden during Riyadh Season. It features interactive songs, dancing, lovable puppets and colorful performances which encourage little ones to sing, play and learn. To learn more, visit enjoy.sa.

item.title: Ancient wonders
item.description: Explore Hegra’s UNESCO-listed landscape on a guided sunset hike through its dramatic sandstone formations, discovering the geological wonders that shaped the Nabataean tombs and monuments and the relationship between nature and human ingenuity. For details, visit experiencealula.com.

item.title: American woman freed after 10 years in Cuba
item.description: A US citizen, Alina Lopez, has been released from detention in Cuba after nearly a decade. Her return was facilitated by American officials without any exchange deal.

item.title: Saudi education minister witnesses 9 agreements with US universities, firms
item.description: WASHINGTON: During his official visit to the US, Minister of Education Yousef Al-Benyan witnessed the signing of nine bilateral cooperation agreements between Saudi educational entities and American universities, institutions and companies.

item.title: Virginia child dies in state’s first measles-associated death of 2026
item.description: VIRGINIA, USA: Virginia reported its first measles-associated death of 2026 on Friday, involving a child who tested positive for measles, the state health department said. The department ⁠said the child ⁠was between 0 and 4 years old.

item.title: Trump says he wants a ‘real deal’ with Iran as escalations rise
item.description: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump told reporters Friday that Tehran wants a deal but not one that is “acceptable” to him.Trump has oscillated between wanting a resolution to the longstanding nuclear issue and saying that the US does not need to make any deal with its longtime adversary.“We want…

item.title: Indian man jailed over US murder plot against Sikh separatist
item.description: NEW YORK: An Indian man was sentenced Friday to more than 19 years in a US prison for plotting to hire a hitman to kill a Sikh separatist on American soil, allegedly on behalf of Indian intelligence.

item.title: Where We Are Going Today: Habibi Hot Pot in Riyadh serves up hearty broths, crisp veggies, tender proteins
item.description: RIYADH: As hot pot restaurants continue to gain popularity in the Saudi capital, Habibi Hot Pot in Olaya offers diners a chance to explore Chinese-style communal dining, where the experience revolves around cooking fresh ingredients in simmering broth at the table.

item.title: What We Are Reading Today: ‘Crossing the Danube’ by Susanne E. Hackenbeck
item.description: “Crossing the Danube” offers a new account of the peoples who lived along Europe’s greatest river—the nearly 2,000-mile-long Danube—during the dramatic centuries leading up to the end of the Roman Empire in the West.

item.title: Can Iraq break the grip of Iran-backed militias without triggering a wider confrontation?
item.description: Amid escalating tensions in Iraq, government forces began asserting control over Jurf Al-Sakher from the Iran-backed militia Kataeb Hezbollah after negotiations, avoiding military confrontation.

item.title: Young protesters hit the streets across Europe
item.description: Protesters across Europe rallied against high living costs, military spending, and climate inaction, pressuring leaders to address young people’s concerns.

item.title: Exam shows that hat Fiona the hippo ate was deep into her small intestine
item.description: CINCINNATI: A necropsy on Fiona the hippo showed that the hat she swallowed nearly two weeks ago was caught in the middle of her small intestine, causing her death this week, the Cincinnati Zoo said Friday.

item.title: Rights groups warn of systematic harm to Palestinian child detainees
item.description: RAMALLAH: Prisoner advocacy groups have warned that Israeli authorities are systematically subjecting Palestinian child detainees to physical and psychological harm. The organizations report that the conflict in Gaza has significantly escalated the targeting of Palestinian youth.

item.title: Scientists are learning more about the rare Ebola virus in Congo outbreak
item.description: Researchers are gaining insights into the rare Bundibugyo strain amid the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, hoping to control its spread.

item.title: Syria, Jordan, Iraq and Lebanon sign agricultural pact to boost food security
item.description: BEIRUT: Syria, Jordan, Iraq and Lebanon have signed an agreement to strengthen agricultural cooperation, improve food security and expand regional trade to address shared challenges in food production and resource management.

item.title: Brazil ex-President Bolsonaro taken to hospital with abdominal pain, son says
item.description: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro has been hospitalized due to severe abdominal pain, a condition related to past injuries from a 2018 stabbing. His son, Carlos Bolsonaro, confirmed this development.

item.title: CONMEBOL reiterates support for Infantino’s FIFA re-election bid
item.description: CONMEBOL has affirmed its unanimous support for Gianni Infantino’s re-election as FIFA president, with backing from all member associations ahead of next year’s election. The decision was made following a council meeting in Barranquilla, Colombia.

item.title: F1 agrees framework for switch to V8 engines from 2030, says FIA
item.description: Formula One is set to switch back to 2.1 liter turbocharged V8 engines in 2030 following an agreement among stakeholders, marking a return to a livelier racing format.

item.title: Rights groups urge sanctions after top UN court finds Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
item.description: UNITED NATIONS: Rights groups are calling for military and economic sanctions against Myanmar after the United Nations’ highest court, in the first ruling of its kind, determined that its government committed genocide against the Rohingya minority in a brutal 2017 military operation.

item.title: Al-Nassr rue Ronaldo penalty miss as Toney fires Al-Ahli to comeback win
item.description: RIYADH: By the 17th minute, it seemed as if Al-Ahli were braced for a high-scoring defeat against Al-Nassr. Cristiano Ronaldo, who had opened the scoring for Al-Nassr with his 986th career goal just three minutes earlier, stepped up to take a penalty, only for his effort to rattle the post.

item.title: 6 weeks before UNIFIL exits Lebanon, Security Council backs mission but no word of a replacement
item.description: NEW YORK CITY: The UN Security Council on Friday reaffirmed its backing for the UN’s peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon, and urged all parties active in the region to protect its personnel.

item.title: Eisenkot vows to bring about new Israeli government swiftly
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot promises a rapid formation of a new Israeli government amid internal divisions over potential alliances. Discussions include whether to collaborate with ultra-Orthodox and Arab-majority parties, or form a unity government with Netanyahu.

item.title: New technology targets heat-related limits on Saudi power lines
item.description: RIYADH: Extreme temperatures can place considerable strain on electricity transmission networks, particularly overhead power lines that must carry rising loads while operating within strict thermal limits.

item.title: Experts hail Saudi Arabia’s top rating in UN digital-government rankings
item.description: RIYADH: Saudi Arabia took first place globally in the UN’s Online Service Index, and was ranked fourth worldwide in its E-Government Development Index for 2026, achievements that experts said reflected the digital transformation in the Kingdom and highlighted the importance of artificial…

item.title: How an OIC-led case made legal history against Myanmar over the Rohingya genocide
item.description: The International Court of Justice has made legal history by ruling, for the first time, that a state—Myanmar—committed genocide against the Rohingya during military operations in 2017.

item.title: Gaza civil defense says Israeli strikes kill six
item.description: Israeli airstrikes in the Gaza Strip resulted in six casualties, as reported by the local civil defense agency. The strikes targeted multiple military operatives despite an existing ceasefire agreement.

item.title: Denmark expels Russian diplomat over attempt to kill Ukrainian rapper
item.description: Denmark has decided to expel a Russian diplomat after suspecting Russia’s involvement in an attempted assassination of a Ukrainian rapper. The Russian ambassador was informed of the decision by Denmark’s foreign minister.

item.title: Cartoon by Amjad Rasmi. (Courtesy of Asharq Al-Awsat)
item.description: Cartoon by Amjad Rasmi. (Courtesy of Asharq Al-Awsat)

item.title: Courtois extends Real Madrid stay with new deal until 2028
item.description: MADRID: Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois has signed a contract extension until June 2028, the LaLiga club said on Friday.

item.title: Former French premier de Villepin launches presidential bid, warns against Le Pen victory
item.description: PARIS: Former French Prime Minister Dominique de Villepin announced his candidacy for president on Friday, invoking Charles de Gaulle’s legacy and pledging to strengthen France’s international standing and defeat political extremism.

item.title: Estonia to close border with Russia, Moscow decries 'new Iron Curtain'
item.description: VILNIUS: Estonia will close its road border crossings with Russia on security grounds for at least six months, the Baltic country's government said on Friday, prompting a warning from Moscow that it would respond with political and diplomatic measures.

item.title: 19 crew members airlifted after cargo ship runs aground in southwestern France
item.description: PARIS: A cargo ship flying the Maltese flag ran aground off the coast of the Landes region in southwestern France amid strong winds early on Friday, leading to the evacuation of 19 crew members by helicopter, local authorities said.

item.title: France probes actor Depardieu, author Houellebecq over alleged rape
item.description: PARIS: French police are investigating allegations actor and convicted sex offender Gerard Depardieu and author Michel Houellebecq gang-raped and assaulted a woman on camera during a 2018 film shoot, two sources following the case said Friday.

item.title: Turkiye opposition slams ruling against Istanbul mayor as ‘cowardice’
item.description: ISTANBUL: Turkiye’s main opposition leader has denounced as “cowardice” a reported court ruling against Istanbul’s jailed mayor which would block him from challenging President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in upcoming elections.

item.title: European troops from 11 countries hold a drill in Poland for a potential postwar Ukraine mission
item.description: NOWA DEBA, Poland: Thousands of European troops are taking part in an unprecedented military exercise in southeastern Poland to prepare for a potential postwar mission in Ukraine aimed at helping to stabilize the country and rebuild its military once the war ends.

item.title: Trump says Putin ‘expressed his desire’ for end of Ukraine war
item.description: US President Donald Trump reported that Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed a desire for a diplomatic end to the Ukraine war during their recent meeting.

item.title: Treasury Secretary Bessent insists US will continue squeezing Iran’s economy
item.description: LONDON: The United States will continue to squeeze Iran’s economy until Tehran “sticks to a deal,” US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday.

item.title: UN cuts food aid target despite looming hunger crisis
item.description: GENEVA: The United Nations food agency said on Friday it plans to assist fewer people in the coming year due to funding constraints even as it warns of a possible global food crisis on the scale of the one that followed the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Poverty, exploitation: Forced into begging on west African streets
item.description: Thousands from Niger are driven by poverty and conflict to beg in West African countries. Human trafficking networks have been exploiting vulnerable individuals through organized begging rings.

item.title: Ukraine child deaths, injuries climb to near 2022 levels, UNICEF says
item.description: The number of children affected by the Ukraine war this year is close to rivaling figures from 2022, with Russian attacks cited as a major cause of casualties, according to UNICEF.

item.title: COP31 deal elusive as fossil fuel fight deepens
item.description: ANTALYA: The UN’s COP31 climate talks were set to spill into overtime Friday as countries remained deadlocked over a draft deal that makes no mention of fossil fuels, with a host of other disputes also snarling negotiations.

item.title: Tunisia rights activist sentenced to five years in prison
item.description: TUNIS: A Tunisian court has sentenced a prominent rights activist to five years in prison on charges of corruption during her tenure as head of a transitional justice commission, her lawyer said Friday.

item.title: Spain face France, England take on Norway in Nations League quarters
item.description: PARIS: World champions Spain will face France while England will play Norway in the quarter-finals of the UEFA Nations League, after the draw took place on Friday. Spain beat France 2-0 in the semifinals of the World Cup in the United States in July, on the way to winning the trophy.

item.title: Yemeni army reports 854 operations against Houthi forces, claims 193 killed or wounded
item.description: ADEN: Yemen’s armed forces say they have carried out 854 operations against Houthi forces across several fronts in recent hours, claiming that 193 field commanders and fighters were killed or wounded.

item.title: Tanker hit in Strait of Hormuz as missile strikes Iran's Qeshm Island
item.description: A tanker ​sailing outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck ‌by ‌an ​unknown ‌projectile, the UK Maritime ⁠Trade Operations (UKMTO) said ‌on ‌Friday The vessel's company security officer had reported ‌a fire on board, the agency said.

item.title: Smith stepping down after almost 17 years as Britain’s Davis Cup captain
item.description: LONDON: Britain’s longest-serving Davis Cup captain Leon Smith will step down after next week’s Finals in Italy, the Lawn Tennis Association confirmed on Friday.

item.title: Kenya investigates deaths of seven hippos
item.description: Kenya is investigating the deaths of seven hippos near Lake Naivasha. The suspected causes are indigestible crops and a fishing net.
